subject: Re: EdgeFin - Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@edgefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + next steps / benchmark materials attached

Alex — great to meet today. Thanks for walking us through EdgeFin's production constraints. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps for the SLO/benchmark work so we can make the pilot efficient: 

Summary of your SLO targets (as discussed) 
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for generation up to 512 tokens (interactive UI)
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s at 512-token average workload
- Concurrency: support for 12-16 concurrent interactive users without tail-latency degradation
- Streaming: yes — partial-token streaming required for the UI to display incremental suggestions

Proposed benchmark scope and deliverables 
1) Reproducible benchmark harness (we'll provide a runnable harness and configs)
2) Shared prompt set (attached: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.json) + your private prompts if you want
3) Measurement definitions doc (attached) — p50/p95/p99, error rate, token throughput, and memory/KV-cache metrics
4) Three runs (cold cache, warm cache, warm cache) with the same harness to measure variance

Attachments included in this email: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.json, redwood_benchmark_harness_v0.3.md, measurement_definitions.md

Next steps / asks 
- Please confirm the SLO targets above or call out any adjustments.
- Confirm a 2-hour window (we suggest next Tue or Wed morning PT) where EdgeFin can give us access to a staging endpoint or allow test traffic (we can also run from our Dedicated env if you prefer).
- If you'd like, Logan (cc'd) will provide a short run-config (harness_run_config.yaml) for the first run.

I'll hold a calendar invite for a 2-hour pilot slot once you confirm availability.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this reproducible benchmark in place.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Redwood attachments: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.json; redwood_benchmark_harness_v0.3.md; measurement_definitions.md

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + next steps / benchmark materials attached

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligned with what we need. A few clarifying questions before we schedule the run: 

1) Streaming: when you say "streaming required," do you have a recommended framing for partial-token latencies? We care about time-to-first-token (TTFT) as much as p95 for full-response. 
2) Load shape: our UI has spikes (bursty arrivals) — can your harness support realistic burst patterns (short high-burst periods followed by quiet windows)?
3) Environment: we'd prefer Redwood to run the initial pass from a Dedicated environment you manage (so results reflect your production serving). Is that OK?

We can do Tue morning PT (10–12 PT). Please confirm the exact start time and whether you need VPN/staging creds. Also — we will share a small set of proprietary prompts and a sanitized dataset for throughput measurement, if that helps.

Alex
Alex Turner | Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeFin
alex.turner@edgefin.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@edgefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:10:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + next steps / benchmark materials attached

Alex — great questions. Answers below and a short plan: 

1) Streaming metrics: we recommend measuring (a) time-to-first-token (TTFT), (b) time-to-50%-tokens, and (c) end-to-end p50/p95/p99 for full response. We'll include TTFT instrumentation in the harness (redwood_benchmark_harness_v0.3.md).

2) Load shape: yes — the harness supports Poisson, bursty (sawtooth) patterns, and recorded traces. Please send a short tsv/csv of your arrival timestamps if you want replay.

3) Environment: running from Redwood Dedicated is OK. We recommend running one validation pass from your staging endpoint (if you can provide access) and the main runs from our Dedicated pool so we can control the environment and collect detailed kernel/hardware traces. Either approach is fine — we just want to capture consistent hardware metadata for reproducibility.

Proposed schedule: Tue 06 Oct 2026 10:00–12:00 PT. Logan will post a harness_run_config.yaml by EOD with recommended concurrency, worker threads, and cache warmup steps. Rishi will be our engineering lead on the run and can jump on the call for troubleshooting.

For reproducibility: please confirm the model variants you want tested (e.g., redwood-70B-quant, redwood-13B-fp16) and whether truncation rules (max tokens) are applied on the client. We'll lock those in the harness config.

Attachments: harness_run_config.yaml (draft will follow), link to shared Drive folder with docs (see related links).

Thanks — confirming calendar once Alex confirms.

—
Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + next steps / benchmark materials attached

Adding a quick technical note on measurement definitions and run hygiene so expectations are clear before the Tue run: 

- Cache warmup: we recommend a 15-min warmup with representative prompts to populate KV cache. Run 1 should be explicitly cold (restart processes / clear caches) to measure cold-start overhead. Runs 2 and 3 should use warm caches.
- Measurement windows: collect per-request metrics (TTFT, p50/p95/p99 response latency) and per-token throughput. Also capture GPU utilization, CPU, and network egress.
- Reproducibility: pin model binary and runtime versions (we'll include exact kernel versions in the harness), fix random seeds where sampling is involved, and record hardware SKU + drivers in the run artifact.
- Concurrency: to match your target of 200 req/s, start with 32 worker threads and a concurrency cap of 16, then sweep concurrency to see tail effects. The harness includes a sweep mode.

Attached sample config: harness_run_config.yaml (basic sweep + warmup + logging). We recommend 3 repeat runs and saving raw event traces (JSONL) for post-run analysis.

If you want, I can join Tue's call and stream the run logs so we can iterate on thresholds in real time.

—
Logan Wright
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
